kernel_events.dependency_inputs: Each selected dependency module records tracked and nonignored untracked file SHA-256 hashes and permission modes, deleted paths and symlink targets plus linked file contents. Gitlinks and directory links recurse, with named cycle rejection; directories without a Git index and uninitialized gitlinks record their empty or locally overridden tree without Git metadata. Only Git's exit-128 not-a-repository diagnostic selects the local-directory fallback; other failures retain their diagnostics and remain errors. Both product and mutation final admission compare this inventory before/after, detecting byte/mode/link drift under identical HEAD/status while accepting unchanged local overrides and ignoring generated caches in Git inventories. Synthetic actual-entry controls cover stock-zmk and dya, tracked/untracked and newline paths, linked contents/targets, nested modules and executable mode; the original entry accepts these changes and fails the named drift assertion. Plain-directory links use real Git for their missing-index response: unchanged inputs pass and edited headers fail on both cores and both run paths; the pre-fallback runner fails all eight named support assertions. These controls establish admission, not firmware behaviour.
kernel_events.baseline_product_reuse: The unchanged baseline may supply that core's normal product evidence only when baseline/results.json covers exactly all cases.json names, every case has three successful repeats with identical nonempty traces, and binary/config/source/dependency identities match. Verify coverage before omitting a separate product build/run. Selected-fault baselines with missing catalogue cases remain focused evidence. The other core requires its own full product result; keep normal results separate from fault rejections.
kernel_events.case_selection: Product --case selections are deduplicated in first-occurrence order before the three repeats, preserving the first stdout/stderr/exit evidence. Mutation expected-case lists must be nonempty and contain no duplicate names; invalid lists are rejected before any baseline or worker build, so a case's evidence is never overwritten by a duplicate selection.
kernel_events.asserts: Exact report contents and order, selected bus transactions, bounds on observed delays, and identical printed traces including raw ticks in input/HID/bus/RDY observations per case in tests/kernel/events/cases.json. Real devicetree instances, I2C emulator, ISR-raised RDY, work and input queues, PM and ZMK listener. Fixture/case-list equality and successful retained list subprocess required. Product runs: both cores, one build at the production 32768 Hz tick rate, every case three times on that binary. Identity covers src, fixture, Kconfig, dts, CMakeLists.txt, zephyr and dependencies.json; dependency selection rechecked after execution. Product admission requires nonempty cases/traces, exactly one whole named completion line, exit 0 and no IQSFAIL. Actual controller flags assert contiguous register writes or repeated-START reads and final STOP; logged RDY edges retain pre-edge driver IRQ-armed state. Accepted but ignored silent-boot resets retry every 200 ms within one budget of three accepted/failed commands; RDY/setup progress stops retries.
kernel_events.negative_control: --negative-control mutations: the unchanged 32768 Hz baseline is an independent retained copy of the first successful worker's pristine binary/config/DTS/CMake/build evidence, with source_worker and SHA-256; it runs concurrently with the --jobs workers (capped by selected fault count), without another build and must pass every case named by the selected faults with three identical-binary repeats for the control to succeed. Empty expected-case lists are rejected before builds. Every worker must finish successfully; pristine-build failures and exceptions with tracebacks are terminal failures recorded in results.json alongside baseline_passed, baseline identity/result/exception, elapsed seconds and mutations. Workers each build a pristine copy once, retaining its SHA-256, .config, zephyr.dts and CMakeCache.txt under worker-N/, then apply one fault at a time, rebuild incrementally, run its named cases and restore the file. Each fault records previous_binary_sha256 before its rebuild and binary_sha256 after a successful rebuild; equality with either the worker's pristine hash or the pre-build hash is STALE-BINARY, fails and skips cases. A previous fault's failing executable cannot reject a new fault. Every non-REJECTED fault retains the available executable; failed rebuild logs remain. Each fault applies with the exact match count within the function body or whole file, must build, and must be rejected by an entire IQSFAIL case=NAME line=NUMBER assertion line and exit 1 from every named case. Timeouts, signals, other exits, similarly named cases, build failures, stale binaries, survivors and faults that never ran fail, reported separately from product runs. All failed pristine builds release the baseline waiter; baseline exceptions are retained and terminal. Separate staging/build/subprocess timing files and fault build/case/total seconds support efficiency comparisons.
kernel_events.output_isolation: Normalize evidence paths before writes; reject owner, workspace and every selected west project root, including aliases and uncloned roots. Existing evidence, source bytes and source directory trees stay untouched. External siblings and safe aliases remain supported. test_runner.py drives the actual entry with synthetic dependencies and builds, including discarded dot-dot components, normalized existing targets and symlink loops. Admission controls also run through tests/test_kernel_event_runner.py in canonical host/CI tests before native builds.
kernel_events.limits: Model only: no capacitive front end, gesture classifier, forced-communication clock stretching, wake reseed, electrical timing/bus, contention, keyboard input processors or elapsed time on a board
kernel_events.model: Datasheet v1.4: programmed 0x32 window timeout discards window gesture flags/pending report while preserving the current sample for forced/verification reads (100 ms assumed before programming; no documented default), STOP ends session, Show Reset gates event mode, bits 9/10 gate gesture/trackpad events, one-cycle re-ATI, suspend after session. Backpressure: 17 accepted reports, ninth contact read blocks, three independently timed-out windows; all 19 produced contact reports, later lift and triple tap delivered in order. Present sensors finish with no contact/verification work and quiet bus; absent sensors at most three boot attempts. Stationary verified-contact backpressure: expired window and due verification during stall; resume gives exactly 21 reports with contact held, then normal lift gives 24. timeout-invents-lift restores zeroing and must be rejected separately as a model control.

kernel.asserts: Actual ordinary/delayed work and full-queue input consumer reject synchronous PM with EWOULDBLOCK before side effects; subsequent external suspend/resume releases the owed button exactly once. A fourth cancel case holds each of five real running workers in turn while external PM blocks in synchronous cancellation, retaining RDY-owned state until its handler returns and delivering exactly one owed release before resume. Four cases x three identical-binary runs per core. Sequential cancellation sync descriptors may share per-instance storage only after each synchronous call returns; the release flush and asynchronous workers retain independent storage. No simultaneous same-device PM action support is claimed. Actual Zephyr conversion comparison at 7 positive rates over all 65536 uint16 waits; existing PM markers and behavior retained.
kernel.negative_control: --negative-control invalid-priority requires named compile rejection; no runtime execution is reported as a passing control. --negative-control early-cancel-state inserts a retry-counter reset before cancellation in an isolated source copy: it must compile and reject all three cancel repeats with exit1 and the named worker-owned-state assertion, separately from product results; build failures, timeouts and unrelated assertions cannot qualify.
kernel.limits: Actual kernel cancellation with GPIO emulation; no physical bus, sensor or downstream transport evidence

timeout_conversion: Two variable touch verification reservations use 32-bit divisions with exact ceiling over the full uint16 range, retaining the tick ABI, zero-disable behavior and all I2C/GPIO/PM/report policy. No retired instrumentation.

raw_tap_cells.asserts: Actual raw32-bit DTS tap cells: explicit <(-1)> means disabled for all3 tap properties; default -1 and valid0/127 stay accepted. Each property rejects -2,128,255,256,65535 with exactly its named compile assertion. Source object compilation uses pinned clean stock/DYA; before repair explicit disabled fails the single-tap assertion on both. No runtime gesture/click/lifecycle logic changed.
